R1114.note: Bounds check now uses segment.size() instead of the forgeable claimedCapacity, matching the contract; param is left unused but harmless.

R1115.note: can:update,order matches the sibling mutating routes and the file's own comment that purge is at least as sensitive as update; no other change.

R1116.note: Only closes the timing side-channel; leaves passwords stored and compared in plaintext, which the file's own comment ('always held...unhashed') flags as the real weakness - the wrong shape for CWE-287 here.

R1117.note: Correct sanitize-then-trust pattern, but the fixed code never imports/requires DOMPurify - as written it throws a ReferenceError on every call, silently breaking all legitimate comment rendering.

R1118.note: Removing ProcessBuilder fully closes CWE-78, but the replacement writes raw, unencoded header data straight into a text/html response, introducing a new reflected XSS not disclosed in the write-up.

R1119.note: Replaces the token-controlled jku resolver with a JWKS fetch from a fixed trusted URL and static IssuerSigningKeys; preserves ValidateToken's throw-on-failure contract.

R1120.note: toRealPath()+startsWith() containment check is solid, but removing the URLDecoder.decode() step is an unstated behavior change (the claim that the container already decodes cookie values is doubtful) that can mangle legitimately percent-encoded filenames.

R1121.note: Switching off libxmljs to fast-xml-parser genuinely closes XXE (the library doesn't resolve external entities at all), but processEntities:false is misdescribed as the XXE defense and actually disables normal &/< entity decoding, an unstated behavior change for ordinary XML content.

R1122.note: Fixed code redeclares 'PreparedStatement sqlStatement' in a scope where 'Statement sqlStatement' is already a local variable from the enclosing method - verified with javac that this is a compile error (duplicate local variable), so it would not build.

R1123.note: json_encode() produces a safe JS string literal for the assignment; preserves the same string value for legitimate input with no other observable change.

R1124.note: strnlen() gate before sscanf correctly prevents the source over-read (the actual root cause per the file's own comment); added %255s width is redundant defense-in-depth that doesn't change legitimate parsing.

R1125.note: html/template auto-escapes Author/Excerpt in the same markup structure; only observable change is escaping of special characters, which is the intended fix.

R1126.note: Correctly recognizes ArgumentList alone doesn't stop cmd.exe's batch-file re-parsing and adds an allowlist regex as the load-bearing defense, stated plainly.

R1127.note: doc.XmlResolver = null is the standard, correct mitigation for XmlDocument.LoadXml XXE; no other observable change.

R1128.note: Allowlist plus path.resolve()+startsWith(pluginsDir+sep) containment check correctly blocks traversal; explicit '.js' suffix matches the file's own stated plugin layout, so no functional regression.

R1129.note: c:out value="${displayName}" cannot see the scriptlet's local Java variable (EL only reads page/request/session/application attributes, not scriptlet locals) - the banner will silently render empty for every user instead of the name, which the write-up doesn't flag.

R1130.note: Only rejects non-http(s) schemes; still allows sendRedirect to any attacker-controlled http(s) host, leaving the core CWE-601 open-redirect open (write-up even defers host allowlisting to 'consider for production'), while the new getHost()==null check also silently breaks legitimate relative-path redirects.
